title: Source-identical basketball foreground coverage mask
status: Final art-side mask solution; supersedes generated foreground and polygon-only proof.
draw_order: Same original hoop RGB at identical transform, alpha multiplied by supplied foreground coverage mask; restrict redraw to ball visible bounding rectangle so unaffected antialiased edges are not composited twice
registration: Exact same source pixels and same transform; no doubled geometry, no resampling between rear and foreground texture.
ball_interaction: Apply foreground redraw only while world ball intersects hoop/net volume. Normal world ordering once ball clears the bottom.

proof.description: Actual static alpha composite using unchanged full hoop, shared ball and source-sampled foreground coverage mask
visual_checks: No purple support covering ball through net openings
Front rim and hanging ropes visibly occlude ball at all three test positions

limits: Material segmentation is approximate, manually inspected in supplied three-stage proof; not claimed perfect for every possible contact position.
Polygon and mask are 2D occlusion art; runtime ordering, collision and ball movement are not implemented.
Original master PNG unchanged; mask is a separate non-destructive asset.
Omit basketball-hoop-front.png, its generated-layer contract and both older proofs from final production delivery.
mask_mode: 8-bit grayscale L; 0 excludes pixel, 255 fully includes pixel

derivation.small_hole_repair: Connected components of mask<128 with fewer than 90 pixels set to 255; preserves small dark knots while leaving mesh openings clear
derivation.registration: Identity, no offset, no scale relative to original full texture
